title: Fear of Missing Out: Drake Reveals FOMO Is a Short Film
text:
Drake Refuses To Let "ICEMAN" Cool Off As The "Shabang" Challenge Takes Over TikTok

Drake confirmed Saturday that Fear of Missing Out, the project he has been quietly teasing since August, is a film, and it arrives Tuesday, September 15 at 9 p.m. ET on YouTube.

Video:

He made it official with an Instagram caption calling it “a not so short film directed and scored by the family,” attached to a teaser that gave fans their first real look at what he has been building.

The clip runs about 25 seconds. A lime green speedboat cuts across open water with a city skyline sitting in the distance, and Drake appears to be the one behind the wheel. A woman narrates over the footage. “What if I told you there were two versions of your life?” she asks, before laying out both paths. In one, you avoid risk, hold back love and end up feeling like you have gone missing from yourself, searching for something you cannot locate. In the other, you find it. The teaser closes on a stark black and white title card.

That is the whole reveal. No plot, no cast, no runtime, no track list.

The Fear of Missing Out rollout started on August 12, when Drake posted a carousel of old family photos captioned “FOMO 2026” and said nothing else. A little over a week later came an image built to look like the back of an old school CD jewel case with the full title across it, paired with a film camera emoji. That one sent fans in two directions at once, because a CD case reads as an album and a camera emoji reads as a visual. Then on September 3 he dropped a black and white graphic with the caption “SEPT 15 YOUTUBE 9PM” and two emojis, an island and a Ferris wheel.

The Ferris wheel was not random. Drake had been spotted filming at the Canadian National Exhibition in Toronto wearing an Iron Man suit, near a Ferris wheel. Then on September 9, footage circulated of him standing on a bright lime green boat at dusk, surrounded by camera cranes, support vessels and a full production crew. Fans connected that shoot to the project on their own. Saturday’s Fear of Missing Out teaser used the exact same boat, which turned all those fan circulated clips into an unofficial first look he never had to pay for.

Before the reveal, the guessing got creative. A deluxe edition. A documentary. Scary Hours 4. A tour announcement. A fourth album on top of the three he already dropped. The one thing almost nobody landed on was a film.

The timing is what makes this feel like a lot. On May 15, Drake released Iceman, Habibti and Maid of Honour at the same time, 43 songs across three projects, with features from Future, 21 Savage, Sexyy Red, Central Cee, Popcaan, PartyNextDoor, Qendresa, Molly Santana, Loe Shimmy, Iconic Savvy and Stunna Sandy. Iceman debuted at number one on the Billboard 200, his fifteenth chart topping album, which moved him past Jay Z for the most number one albums by a rapper. It has since spent a career best 13 weeks at number one on the Top Rap Albums chart. “Janice STFU” became his fourteenth number one on the Hot 100, breaking a tie with Michael Jackson for the most by a male soloist, and he put a record 42 songs on the chart in a single week.

So Fear of Missing Out is landing four months after all of that, and the man has not slowed down once.

The open question is whether there is new music inside it. Drake has not announced Fear of Missing Out as an album or a single, and the teaser does not hint at a release. But “scored by the family” is doing some work in that caption. You do not score a film with nothing, and Drake’s inner circle has produced every era of his catalog. Whether that means original songs, instrumental cues or something already sitting in the vault, he is not saying.

He rarely does say, which is the point. Promoting Iceman, he put an ice sculpture standing 25 feet tall in a Toronto parking lot and let people figure it out. This time he let a title, a CD case, an Iron Man suit and a boat do the talking for a full month. Fear of Missing Out is the name of the project and it is also, pretty clearly, the strategy.
